title: Northgate Card Courtesy Late Fee Reversal — Qualification and Amount
content:
**The courtesy late fee.** On a **Northgate Card Credit Accounts (issued by Harbor Point Bank, N.A.)** account the courtesy late fee is the most recent late fee recorded on the account, and of two posted the same day the one entered first in the account history; its standing part is the fee less every reversal already posted against it, never less than zero; it is a qualifying courtesy late fee when it is the only late fee recorded on the account in the last 12 months, no courtesy reversal was posted on the account in that time, and at least 1.00 of it still stands.

**Windows.** A count or total over the last 12 or 24 months takes the entries dated after the same calendar day 12 or 24 months before today.

**The amount.** The courtesy reversal is 25 percent of the standing part of the courtesy late fee, rounded half up to the cent. The courtesy share is 25 percent together with every point this rule grants, never above 100 percent, and the courtesy reversal is that share of the standing part of the courtesy late fee, rounded half up to the cent; each point counts as one percentage point of the share.

| Qualifying test (all must hold) | Holds when |
|---|---|
| only late fee in the last 12 months | exactly one late fee is recorded on the account in that time, and it is the courtesy late fee |
| no courtesy reversal in that time | no courtesy reversal was posted on the account in the last 12 months |
| something still stands | at least 1.00 of the courtesy late fee stands after the reversals already posted against it |

## Worked figures (hypothetical late fees)

- A qualifying late fee of 32.00 with no reversal against it: 25 percent of 32.00 is 8.00.
- A qualifying late fee of 43.00 with no reversal against it: 25 percent of 43.00 is 10.75.
- A qualifying late fee with 30.10 still standing: 25 percent is 7.525, rounded half up to 7.53.
- A late fee with 0.80 still standing after a reversal does not qualify: nothing is reversed under this rule.
- A late fee that is the second late fee recorded in the last 12 months does not qualify.
